properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.7 (declared at front/pnpm-lock.yaml:4784) is a transitive dep of the Ethereum wallet stack (elliptic/ethers) and ships SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512. The build ships these hash functions; no direct import in front/src. D-rating driven by SHA-1 availability; hashes are Grover-only, not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @stablelib/poly1305 + @stablelib/chacha20poly1305 1.0.1 are transitive deps of @walletconnect/utils@2.10.2 and 2.10.5 (lock lines 3203, 3236, 2262-2269, 2322) — the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD/Poly1305 MAC that WalletConnect uses to encrypt relay messages. No direct application call site in front/src; presence is the inventory question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-time transitive dependency (via listhen@1.5.5, the Next.js dev-server HTTPS helper); the application's shipped code never imports node-forge (grep over front/src finds no forge import). Changeable here only by dropping the dev dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.2.0 provides secp256k1 ECDSA for the viem/wagmi Ethereum stack (transaction/message signing in the wallet UI). Transitive dep; the secp256k1 curve is Shor-vulnerable but used here for a smart-wallet frontend.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live dependency of the app's WalletConnect stack. Changeable only by the WalletConnect SDK (observable here, replaceable by the vendor) — the app cannot swap the pairing crypto without forking the SDK.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: WalletConnect relay-authentication signing (JWTs signed with Ed25519 client keys for the IRN relay). Live in the app's WalletConnect service; replaceable only by the SDK vendor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: viem's elliptic-curve library. The application exercises secp256k1 through it (relayer signing, filed separately); Ed25519 itself has no application call site — library-level availability in the shipped tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 (front/pnpm-lock.yaml:4017) ships ECDSA over secp256k1/P-256 for the wallet stack. Transitive dep; the ES256 WebAuthn path also relies on P-256 ECDSA (see front/src/libs/web-authn/service/web-authn.ts pubKeyCredParams).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.2.0 ships secp256r1 (P-256) ECDSA/ECDH. This is not merely bundled — the application actively selects ES256 WebAuthn credentials (front/src/libs/web-authn/service/web-authn.ts:61-63) whose P-256 signatures are parsed and pushed to the smart-account factory, so P-256 is an in-use signature scheme here, not just a vendored one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 also provides ECDH key agreement (ecdh over secp256k1/P-256); declared transitively in the lockfile, no direct application call site found. Shor-vulnerable key-agree primitive shipping with the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: six keccak/keccak256 entries (e.g. keccak: 3.0.4 at lock line 226 under @metamask/eth-sig-util, '@ethersproject/keccak256': 5.7.0 at line 424) — SHA-3/Keccak-256 hashing that underpins every Ethereum address and tx hash. Grover-only exposure; kept because the build ships and uses it constantly via the viem stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @stablelib/hkdf@1.0.1 entries (lock lines 2296, 3204, 3227) — HKDF used by @walletconnect/utils@2.10.2/2.10.5 to derive symmetric keys for relay message encryption. No direct application call; presence recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-time transitive dependency via listhen@1.5.5; the shipped application never calls it. Changeable here only by dropping the dev dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: viem's hash library, live in the dependency tree. The application separately hashes SHA-256 on-chain in WebAuthn verification (contracts/src/WebAuthn.sol:164-165, filed as a finding); WalletConnect pulls @stablelib/sha256 for its session crypto. PQ-safe hash — no migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library-level availability inside viem's hash library; PQ-safe hash, no migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes@1.3.2 ships SHA-3/Keccak plus SHA-256; transitive dep of the viem Ethereum stack. Grover-only exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AEAD protecting WalletConnect relay/session traffic. PQ-safe symmetric; the quantum exposure of the WC channel is its X25519 key agreement (filed as a use-site finding at wallet-connect.ts:74). Replaceable only by the SDK vendor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure reference (class 7): not installed, not used, changeable only by the WalletConnect vendor and Microsoft. The relevant posture question — which algorithms the vault would support if enabled — is decided by the Azure service, observable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The app's primary hash library (reached through viem). Which algorithms the app actually invokes is the use-site layer, covered by the findings filed for this hunt.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: viem's curve backend; the relayer's secp256k1 signing path (front/src/app/api/users/save/route.ts:9, filed as a finding) runs through it. Also the source of the X25519/P-256 implementations should application code ever call them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @peculiar/asn1-x509@2.3.8 (lock lines 965/974/995/2205) — X.509 certificate ASN.1 schemas used by the WebAuthn/COSE attestation parsing stack (@peculiar/asn1-schema, @peculiar/asn1-ecc are direct deps in package.json).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Correct CSPRNG choice in a security context: Node's crypto.randomBytes(16) generates the WebAuthn user.id (credential handle). Quantum-safe randomness. Note the contrast: the WebAuthn challenge in the same file is a hardcoded literal string, not randomBytes — see separate finding for that posture issue.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive SHA-2 hashing dependency of the web3 provider stack; no application call site — presence in the shipped tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 (front/pnpm-lock.yaml:4017) — classic ECDSA/ECDH library of the Ethereum wallet stack; no direct import in the application but ships secp256k1 signing to the build. Known-vintage crypto library worth tracking for the migration plan.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hash backend of the transitive elliptic@6.5.4 dependency; no application call site — presence in the shipped tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.3.1 (front/pnpm-lock.yaml:5311, 5571) bundles RSA, TLS, X.509 and PKCS implementations. Transitive dep (WalletConnect/websocket stack), no direct import in front/src — but the image ships these Shor-vulnerable primitives, and node-forge has a history of crypto CVEs, so it belongs in the inventory.
